findings.quote:
br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC);

	nla_for_each_nested(attr, br_spec, rem) {
findings.reason: Untrusted source: userspace RTM_SETLINK (PF_BRIDGE) netlink message; IFLA_AF_SPEC is policy-optional (net/core/rtnetlink.c ifla_policy line 1869: [IFLA_AF_SPEC] = { .type = NLA_NESTED }, no NLA_F_NET...required flag; nlmsg_find_attr returns NULL when absent). rtnl_bridge_setlink (net/core/rtnetlink.c:4886-4921) guards its own br_spec with 'if (br_spec)' but then forwards the raw nlh to dev->netdev_ops->ndo_bridge_setlink(dev, nlh, flags, extack) on the BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF path (line 4920). Violated invariant: i40e_ndo_bridge_setlink (i40e_main.c:12762-12777) fetches br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC) at line 12774 and passes it to nla_for_each_nested(attr, br_spec, rem) at line 12776 with NO 'if (!br_spec)' guard — unlike sibling drivers bnxt.c:12461, be_main.c:4982, ixgbe_main.c:9898, mlx5 en_main.c:4536 which all have it. Unsafe use: nla_for_each_nested expands to nla_for_each_attr(pos, nla_data(nla), nla_len(nla), rem) (include/net/netlink.h:1931-1932), dereferencing NULL br_spec. Consequence: NULL-pointer dereference oops (local DoS) from an attacker-crafted RTM_SETLINK message that includes IFLA_BRIDGE_FLAGS=BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF but omits IFLA_AF_SPEC, targeting an i40e PF VSI (vsi->seid == pf->vsi[pf->lan_vsi]->seid passes the EOPNOTSUPP gate). Counterevidence checked: all other ndo_bridge_setlink implementors and both rtnl_bridge_* dispatchers guard the attribute before use.

findings.quote:
br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC);

	nla_for_each_nested(attr, br_spec, rem) {
findings.reason: Same mechanism: ice_bridge_setlink (ice_main.c:6636-6653) fetches br_spec = nlmsg_find_attr(nlh, sizeof(struct ifinfomsg), IFLA_AF_SPEC) at line 6651 and passes it directly to nla_for_each_nested(attr, br_spec, rem) at line 6653 with no NULL check. nla_for_each_nested dereferences its nesting attribute via nla_data()/nla_len() (include/net/netlink.h:1931-1932), so br_spec == NULL from an attacker-crafted RTM_SETLINK/PF_BRIDGE message (IFLA_AF_SPEC is optional in ifla_policy; the rtnl_bridge_setlink dispatcher at net/core/rtnetlink.c:4920 forwards raw nlh to ndo_bridge_setlink for BRIDGE_FLAGS_SELF) causes a NULL-pointer dereference oops. Counterevidence checked: of the six nlmsg_find_attr(IFLA_AF_SPEC) consumers in this snapshot only i40e (line 12774) and ice (line 6651) lack the 'if (!br_spec) return -EINVAL;' guard; bnxt, be2net, ixgbe, mlx5 and both rtnl_bridge_* dispatchers guard it.

candidates.reason: rtnl_bridge_setlink(): br_spec guarded by 'if (br_spec)' before nla_for_each_nested; final memcpy(nla_data(attr),...) runs only under 'if (have_flags)' which implies attr was set by the guarded loop.
rtnl_bridge_dellink(): identical guarded structure; the only ndo_bridge_dellink implementor (bridge br_dellink, br_netlink.c:1046-1050) returns 0 when afspec is absent.
bnxt_bridge_setlink(): 'if (!br_spec) return -EINVAL;' at lines 12461-12462 before nla_for_each_nested.
be_ndo_bridge_setlink(): 'if (!br_spec) return -EINVAL;' at lines 4982-4983 before nla_for_each_nested.
ixgbe_ndo_bridge_setlink(): 'if (!br_spec) return -EINVAL;' at lines 9898-9899 before nla_for_each_nested.
mlx5e_bridge_setlink(): 'if (!br_spec) return -EINVAL;' at lines 4536-4537 before nla_for_each_nested.

br_setlink(): protinfo/afspec jointly guarded ('if (!protinfo && !afspec) return 0') and each use re-checks presence ('if (p && protinfo)', 'if (afspec) err = br_afspec(...)'), so neither NULL reaches nla_parse_nested_deprecated/nla_get_u8.
neigh_delete(): dst_attr = nlmsg_find_attr(..., NDA_DST) immediately checked with 'if (!dst_attr) ... goto out' before any nla_len/nla_data use.
qeth_l2_bridge_setlink(): iterates top-level attrs with nlmsg_for_each_attr and gates bp_tb[] usage behind has_protinfo ('if (!has_protinfo) return 0'); IFLA_PROTINFO only parsed when present.

do_setlink()/rtnl_setlink tb[] consumption (IFLA_* slots are optional in ifla_policy by default) was only pattern-surveyed; the per-kind rtnl_link_ops changelink sweep across ~60 kind files was not completed within this intent's bounds and is left to the tb[]-audit branch.

limitations: Only the RTM_SETLINK/RTM_DELLINK bridge attribute paths driven by nlmsg_find_attr were fully audited (all six IFLA_AF_SPEC consumer sites plus the rtnl_bridge_setlink/dellink dispatchers); the ~60 rtnl_link_ops per-kind newlink/changelink handlers were pattern-grepped but not individually read, so a tb[]-slot gap inside a specific kind's changelink could remain unreported here.

Whether an unprivileged user without CAP_NET_ADMIN can reach the rtnl_bridge_setlink doit dispatch in this snapshot (netlink_rcv_skb -> rtnetlink_rcv_msg permission path) was not re-verified line-by-line; the NULL-deref itself is unconditional once the handler is entered.

The two reported findings require the corresponding NIC driver (i40e or ice) with a device in the vulnerable state (e.g., i40e PF VSI); impact on such hardware is a static hypothesis, not a runtime reproduction.
br_setlink's legacy-binary compat path (protinfo without NLA_F_NESTED) reads nla_get_u8(protinfo) after an nla_len check — read as safe, but not compile-tested.
